newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes easier at $342.80, follows PGMs.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes easier at $342.80, follows PGMs.

text.p: Platinum group metal (PMG) prices hit fresh high levels on Wednesday morning but they turned lower later as the surge encouraged profit taking, dealers said.
A slightly firmer dollar following latest U.S. economic data also weighed against the markets.
Palladium fixed this morning at an all-time high of $188.00 per ounce but was marked down to $185.00 at the 1300 GMT fixing and platinum came off a nine-month high of $404.50 to $399.50.
Gold which has lagged the PGMs for weeks was also slightly easier against the morning fix at $342.80 down from $344.70. The June Comex contract was down $1.30 at $343.40.
Gold briefly rose towards its $345.00 resistance, also the most significant strike price of the outgoing over the counter (OTC) options which expired today.
Dealers said the push for the resistance was half hearted and the price fell on a sell-off of option related positions.
The platinum-gold spread which stretched to a premium of around $60 over gold earlier on Wednesday, was not helping gold.
"Nobody believes gold can rise significantly and platinum is too expensive to take risks with," a dealer said.
The gold price's inability to offer support to platinum was one reason speculators took platinum profits after it had broken above $400.00 where it failed on Tuesday, dealers said.
Dealers said business was cautious as they watched for any comments on Germany's plans to revalue its gold reserves following Wednesday's meeting of the Bundesbank Council.
Techncial analysts forecast further pressure for gold now that its nearby support at $343.30 was slipping.
Prices of the PGMs surged to fresh high levels on news of an unofficial strike at a major mine in South Africa.
"The prices have more to do with the very tight physical position of the markets rather than Rustenburg," one dealer said referring to the scramble to buy or borrow either metal.
Their scarcity results from Russia the largest palladium exporter and second biggest platinum supplier after South Africa failing to export this year due to administrative problems.
That pushed the cost of borrowing the metals to 41 percent for palladium and 17 percent platinum this week, dealers said.
"The price is not going to come back down dramatically while the market is this tight," a platinum dealer said.
Silver was straddling support at $4.69/$4.71, down five cents.
